ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human reviewer (Trust & Safety) with the case file: read the rider's complaint allegation that the driver said he knows where she lives and that she should just pay, and decide whether a SAFE-1/SAFE-2 safety violation occurred; if a violation is found, the interim suspension path under SAFE-4 applies, and if none is found, the fare question resolves to no_action (charged $11.81 is $0.50 below the $12.31 quote on an unchanged 1.3× multiplier). Do not action any refund or fee in the meantime; no account flag on the driver (no repeat deviation on record) and no goodwill credit.
ruling.reasoning:
The fare side of this case is settled and yields nothing. The multiplier was 1.3× at quote and 1.3× at trip start [F4][F6][F7][F8], so the SURGE-2 "surge rose, rider not notified" row cannot be triggered by its own terms (the trace marks it ✗) [SURGE-2]. SURGE-3's differential (actual fare − quote) is therefore not "attributable solely to a surge multiplier change": (1.3 − 1.3) × $8.51 = $0.00 [SURGE-3]. The metered build-up matches FARE-0 — $3.90 base + $3.29 distance + $0.93 time + $1.25 platform, with the platform fee not surged — totalling $11.81, which is $0.50 below the $12.31 quote [F5][F6][F7][FARE-0]. The rider has conceded this arithmetic, and F9 ("not notified of the surge change") describes a change that the fare records show never occurred, so it cannot found a dollar award [F9][SURGE-1][SURGE-2].

There is likewise no route element. Billed distance 2.3 km is 0.1 km shorter than the 2.4 km optimal route [F1][F3], well inside RD-1's 1 km tolerance, and the trip (3.6 min) was shorter than the 4.8 min estimate [F2][F3][RD-1]. Nothing is refundable under RD-2, and no driver violation arises on the route [RD-1][RD-2]. Segment_findings is accordingly empty.

The case is removed from the system by the safety screen. The filed complaint states that when the rider asked the driver about pricing, he said he knows where she lives and she had better just pay, and that she felt unsafe for the rest of the ride [F13, rider complaint text]. That is an intimidation allegation made in the course of the trip and is a safety indicator that must go to a person, whatever the dispute type [SAFE-1]. The chat log is complete and timestamped but contains only the pickup note and the car description, with no pricing exchange [F10][F11][F12], and the driver's written statement addresses pricing and route only, denying nothing [F13]; the driver's account is corroborated on route by the GPS track [F1][F2]. I therefore read the allegation as made but not corroborated — "suspected", and expressly not a finding of fact against either party.

Because safety is engaged, SAFE-3 bars me from ruling, assigning fault or recommending an outcome [SAFE-3]; the trace's allowed outcomes of no_action and escalate leave escalate open, and I take it. The amount is null: nothing was overcharged on the fare [F5][F6][F7][F8] and no fee or credit clause applies. The profiles (rider 5.0, 0 upheld; driver 4.58, 0 upheld) engage neither RD-6 nor NS-9 nor the TH-3 fraud threshold and never decide the case [F14][F15][RD-6][TH-3]; the record itself is complete (timestamped messages [F12], full GPS and fare data [F1]–[F9]), so the escalation rests on the safety screen, not on a missing record [TH-4].
